findings.reason: The rest-frame spatial equation contains no b term, so matching it forces a=G only. Step 3.1 infers a+b=1 from orthogonality preservation, but the Statement does not make preservation a condition of the coefficient-matching claim. State the joint conditions or remove the b-uniqueness claim.

The comparison uses a rest frame, spatial components s and B, and an oriented spatial basis without defining them. Specify the pointwise basis with e0=U/c, its positive-definite rest space and spatial orientation, and define the components used in Fij=epsilon_ijk Bk.

j is called Lebesgue-integrable and its vector integral is used, but vector integrability and integration are not defined. State that the components are in L1 and vector integrals are componentwise; define the closed Euclidean ball as {|x|<=ell}.

The Statement uses rest-frame components and an observer-coordinate decomposition without specifying the frame. State the inertial orthonormal frame with time axis p/(Mc) and its oriented spatial basis, or give an equivalent pointwise construction.

The curved clause’s phrase “T has support on Sigma” can mean spacetime support on a hypersurface, which would force a smooth field to vanish. Specify compact support of the restriction T|Sigma. Define Sigma as a C1 embedded spacelike hypersurface, identify its future unit normal and induced volume measure, and cite the inertial-frame/chart definition used in the flat clause.

The exterior field and integral use r and |x| without specifying their common origin or defining ell as the body’s radius in the rest chart. State the center, rest-frame spatial coordinates, r=|x|, and the boundary/support meaning of ell.

The exact-solution Statement does not say that s_parallel and s_perp are the projections of s(tau0). Proof step 1.3 also drops the sine/cosine factors when differentiating; show the derivative as -omega sin(theta) s_perp,0 - omega cos(theta) Bhat cross s_perp,0.

Proof step 2.1 sets e=T00 and j^i=T0i/c and cites the body-moment formula, but no T is supplied in this theorem. The Statement already gives the spin-density equality; use it as stipulated data and remove that derivation, or supply T and define e,j from its rest components.

Proof step 2.1 infers S remains zero from the constant scalar S_ab S^ab/2 alone. That norm is indefinite on arbitrary Lorentzian bivectors. Use the preserved TD constraint to show S is spatial in p’s rest frame, where the norm is positive definite, then infer S=0 from its zero initial norm.
